name: Strained lanthanum calcium manganite
equilibrium_context: A ferromagnetic metal when unstrained; under epitaxial strain tuned into an emergent charge-ordered insulating phase

driven_states.emergent_property: Extreme photosusceptibility: a single optical pulse switches the material into a long-lived, metastable hidden metallic phase. A critical absorbed photon density is required, which activates local charge excitations that mediate magneto-lattice coupling.
driven_states.source: Zhang et al., Nature Materials 15, 956 (2016), doi:10.1038/nmat4695
further_sources: McLeod et al., Nature Materials 19, 397 (2020), doi:10.1038/s41563-019-0533-y (multi-messenger nanoprobes of hidden magnetism in a strained manganite)
driven_states.caveat: The single-shot methodology rules out cumulative heating - a strong argument against a purely thermal origin, and methodologically the cleanest demonstration of metastability in the registry. The authors, however, describe the mechanism as cooperative via magneto-lattice coupling, not as a purely electronic Mott collapse. The photosusceptibility is a strain-engineering effect, not an intrinsic material property - transferability to unstrained material is not established.

sources: Zhang et al., Nature Materials 15, 956 (2016), doi:10.1038/nmat4695
gaps: The critical absorbed photon density is documented, but the numerical value has not been verified against the full text.
